title: Lifting a residue class while avoiding finitely many prime ideals
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with identity, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_r$ prime ideals of $A$ (equivalently, points of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]), where $r\geq0$. Here an ideal is an additive subgroup stable under multiplication by elements of $A$, and a prime ideal is a proper ideal $\mathfrak p$ such that $ab\in\mathfrak p$ implies $a\in\mathfrak p$ or $b\in\mathfrak p$. Suppose $I\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_i$ for every $1\leq i\leq r$. For every residue class $\bar f\in A/I$ (a coset for the additive subgroup $I$) there exists $f\in A$ such that $f+I=\bar f$ and $f\notin\mathfrak p_i$ for every $i$. Repeated or comparable primes, the empty family, and the zero ring are allowed.

source.place: Tag 09NK, label lemma-extra-silly, statement and proof.

proof.text: Discard repeated primes and primes strictly contained in another listed prime. Every discarded prime is contained in a retained one: repeatedly move to a strictly larger listed prime, which must terminate in the finite set. Thus avoiding all retained primes avoids every original prime. Relabel the retained primes $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_t$; they are pairwise incomparable and still satisfy $I\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_i$. Choose a representative $a\in A$ of the coset $\bar f$. If $t=0$, take $f=a$. This also covers the zero ring, which has no proper prime ideal.

Put $S=\{s\in\{1,\ldots,t\}:a\in\mathfrak p_s\}$ and $T=\{1,\ldots,t\}\setminus S$. If $S=\varnothing$, take $f=a$. Otherwise let $J=I\cap\bigcap_{i\in T}\mathfrak p_i$, with the empty intersection understood as $A$. It is an ideal, since each factor contains $0$ and is closed under subtraction and multiplication by any element of $A$. This intersection can replace the product ideal used in Tag 09NK: the following explicit witnesses establish precisely the noncontainment needed there.

For each $s\in S$, choose $u_s\in I\setminus\mathfrak p_s$ using the hypothesis on $I$. For every $i\in T$ choose $v_{i,s}\in\mathfrak p_i\setminus\mathfrak p_s$, using incomparability. Then $z_s=u_s\prod_{i\in T}v_{i,s}$ belongs to $J$: it is a multiple of $u_s\in I$ and, for each $i\in T$, a multiple of $v_{i,s}\in\mathfrak p_i$. It is outside $\mathfrak p_s$, since repeated use of the defining prime implication would otherwise put one of its factors in $\mathfrak p_s$. For $T=\varnothing$ the product is $1$ and $z_s=u_s$. Therefore $J\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_s$ for every $s\in S$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] to the ideal $J$ in $A$ and the nonempty finite family $(\mathfrak p_s)_{s\in S}$. Its noncontainment hypothesis is Step 3; every member of the family is prime, so in particular all but at most two are prime. Obtain $g\in J$ with $g\notin\mathfrak p_s$ for every $s\in S$.

Take $f=a+g$. Because $g\in J\subseteq I$, its coset is $f+I=a+I=\bar f$. If $s\in S$ and $f\in\mathfrak p_s$, then $g=f-a\in\mathfrak p_s$, contrary to Step 4. If $i\in T$ and $f\in\mathfrak p_i$, then $a=f-g\in\mathfrak p_i$, since $g\in J\subseteq\mathfrak p_i$, contrary to the definition of $T$. Thus $f$ avoids the retained primes, and Step 1 gives avoidance of the entire original family.
